title: Harborline Retail — Launch readiness & access check
summary: Kickoff to validate access, security checklist and pilot success criteria ahead of Harborline's sandbox pilot. Confirmed SSO, network peering options, pilot traffic profile, and next steps for benchmarking and data retention. Agreed on timeline for pilot: run 2-week load window starting 6/22, Redwood to share runbook and security pack.
action_items: Maya Thompson: Share pilot runbook, pricing worksheet, and staging access (due 2026-06-09)
Priya Kapoor: Schedule and run a 30-min benchmark with Harborline's sample prompts; capture p95 latency and KV cache behavior (due 2026-06-18)
Jonas Rivera: Provide VPC peering CIDR ranges and point-of-contact for networking (due 2026-06-10)
Simone Batiste: Send SOC 2 and encryption/KMS questions to Redwood security (due 2026-06-11)
next_steps: Redwood to provision sandbox tenant and share credentials in SSO test mode
Customer to ingest 10k sample requests and schedule benchmark window week of 6/22
Security follow-up: exchange compliance docs and confirm encryption-at-rest key management process
transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-06-06 11:00 PT
Duration: ~32 minutes
Attendees: Maya, Daniel, Priya — Harborline: Leah, Jonas, Simone, Evan

Auto-summary (auto): Quick kickoff to confirm who does what for the pilot, access, and security.

00:00 Maya: hey everybody thanks for making the time, quick note we wanted to keep this tight 30 mins — just align on access and security and agree on pilot window
00:15 Leah: thanks Maya, appreciate it. We're excited to get the sandbox going. High level we've got two goals: one proof of latency and cost for customer-facing chat, two validate the private data handling for order history.
00:28 Jonas: yeah and also run the integration with our event pipeline, we want to see embedding latency when we call for product retrieval.
00:40 Daniel: cool, so we'll cover access, network, security, and Priya will talk benchmarks and runbook.
00:48 Priya: hi team, quick note on bench approach: we usually mirror your traffic profile — bursty search-like queries, 95th p latency target, and a mix of embed + generation. we'll test both hosted and dedicated variants unless you'd like to lock to one.
01:05 Simone: question — our compliance team prefers VPC peering or private link, can Redwood do peering into our AWS account? Also key management concerns: we need to keep keys in our KMS/HSM.
01:20 Priya: yes, both options are supported. for Redwood Private we can do VPC peering or customer-managed VPC with a private control plane. for KMS/HSM we integrate with customer KMS for encryption keys, there are a couple of patterns — we can share the security doc.
01:40 Jonas: is there any additional latency we should expect with KMS calls or will it be transparent?
01:47 Priya: good question — KMS calls are async for some of our wider flows, but for token encryption/decryption at model inference time we keep keys cached and avoid an extra roundtrip. you might see a small bump during key rotation windows but normally negligible.
02:05 Evan: cost wise we need a rough estimate — we're budgeting for around $2k/mo for the pilot, is that realistic for 1M tokens?
02:13 Maya: pricing worksheet will show a few options; hosted is easiest to start and generally lower up‑front; dedicated gives better throughput per dollar if you have steady traffic. we'll send the worksheet after this call.
02:30 Leah: for pilot success criteria — we'd like p95 latency under 200ms for short chat turns, embedding lookup under 150ms, and no customer data leaving our VPC. also minimal degradations during peak promo periods.
02:48 Daniel: makes sense. we'll include those metrics in the runbook and the health dashboard in Redwood Console — you'll get token-level cost and latency breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and tracing hooks.
03:05 Simone: can we get audit logs forwarded to our SIEM? we need to keep logs for 12 months and keep them in our account ideally.
03:15 Priya: yes, we can forward logs to your S3 or syslog endpoint. retention is configurable; default retention in hosted is shorter but for Private we can pipe everything to your bucket.
03:29 Jonas: network-wise we'll send you the CIDR range and the platform team, but what's the typical required throughput for the benchmark nodes?
03:36 Priya: for the benchmark we usually ask for a sandbox with 4 concurrent threads simulating your peak qps, but we can tune. if you expect bursty spikes, we'll use continuous batching options and show how batching impacts latency vs cost.
03:52 Leah: we have an existing embeddings pipeline that uses 1536-d vectors, want to know if Redwood supports that size and quantized embeddings for cheaper vector store space.
04:03 Priya: yes we support multiple embedding dims; quantization recommendations are part of Redwood Optimize toolkit. we'll include model/quantization suggestions for your workload in the runbook.
04:15 Simone: SOC 2 questions — do you have an SOC 2 report and can we get a copy under NDA? Also SSO — we use Okta, can you do SAML SSO and SCIM for user sync?
04:28 Maya: yes, SOC 2 is available for customers under NDA, we also support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning. we'll connect your security contact with our security team after this call.
04:44 Evan: small thing — do you support feature flags or A/B routing for rollouts? we want to test a smaller model for cost saving on low-value customers.
04:53 Daniel: yep Redwood supports canary rollouts and routing policies, automatic fallback to a cheaper model variant if needed. Console has A/B routing controls and per-route dashboards.
05:08 Jonas: when we talk about dedicated capacity is that a full GPU reservation or is it pooled? how do bursts work?
05:18 Priya: Dedicated is reserved GPU pools; you can configure burst capacity so traffic beyond the reservation can spike up using burstable capacity. there are autoscale policies that respect your latency SLOs.
05:30 Leah: any gotchas for private on‑prem deployments? network latency to our data center is a risk — we might prefer a hybrid approach where the control plane is separate from runtime.
05:42 Priya: that's common — hybrid where control plane is hosted and runtime sits in your VPC or on-prem is a pattern. we provide metrics endpoints and tracing to help debug latency.
05:55 Simone: regarding PII, can we have redactors or token filters before data leaves our systems?
06:02 Priya: yes you can add pre-processing — Redwood supports pre-commit filters, prefix stripping, and on-the-fly redaction hooks. we'll include an example lambda in the runbook.
06:15 Maya: timeline check — customer wants pilot start late June; are we comfortable with a 2-week benchmarking window starting 2026-06-22?
06:24 Leah: that works as long as we have credentials and security handshake by 6/10.
06:30 Maya: perfect. Priya you'll run the bench and share results, Simone we'll route security sync.
06:36 Priya: yes, I'll schedule a 45-minute bench run and invite Jonas to watch.
06:42 Jonas: cool, sample data — we'll provide 10k prompts and a small set of order-history records for privacy testing.
06:49 Daniel: on the observability side we'll give you a dashboard link and a short guide to interpret cost vs latency graphs.
06:55 Leah: any obstacles you foresee with our infra? we run multi-AZ in us-east-1 and have strict egress rules.
07:03 Priya: we'll need a temporary peering config and a break-glass plan for maintenance windows, otherwise it's straightforward.
07:12 Simone: can we get a brief runbook of SSR and incident response? we need SLAs for support and escalation path.
07:20 Maya: yes, we'll include escalation matrix and SLA options in the pricing doc, plus a 24/7 escalation contact for enterprise tiers.
07:29 Evan: and for demo metrics — can Redwood emit synthetic traffic so we can see behavior before we send real data?
07:37 Priya: yes, we can run synthetic through the staged tenant and show how caching and batching work, including KV cache hit/miss stats.
07:46 Maya: ok let me recap next steps, action owners — Maya will send pricing and runbook by 6/9; Priya will schedule bench and run on 6/22 window; Jonas will send network details by 6/10; Simone will consolidate security Qs and send to Redwood security by 6/11.
07:58 Leah: sounds good, thanks everyone.
08:02 Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up in email with the links: runbook (link), security pack (link), and a staging URL.
08:10 Priya: one more quick note — there might be slight transcription of some product names here, "Redwood Dedicate" sometimes appears in docs. full name is Redwood Dedicated and Redwood Private, will make sure doc uses correct names.
08:21 Meeting end

References and links mentioned (sent later):
- Pilot runbook (internal link)
- Security pack & SOC 2 (NDA required)
- Pricing worksheet and SLA options
- Staging tenant dashboard link
notes: Customer asked specifically for KV cache stats, embedding dims review, and SSO/SCIM details. Agreed pilot start and owners. Security NDA required before SOC2 share.
